Produce an executable realignment plan for a feature branch, from a verified divergence register.

READ FIRST: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plans/sfcc-89-realignment-register.md — every row in it has been independently reproduced from source. Treat it as established fact; do not re-litigate the findings. Read the cited files to design the fix, not to re-audit.

REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
BRANCH: `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`, at develop's tip `8362b3c` (PR #59 merged), with **29 staged, uncommitted files** — `git diff --cached --name-only`. There are no commits on the branch.

CURRENT STATE — all green: `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors · `npx vitest run` 354 tests · Storybook `test-storybook --ci` 100 tests / 22 suites · `npm run lint` 17 errors, exactly develop's pre-existing baseline · `npm run audit:tokens` 19 unacknowledged (14 develop, 5 ours).

THE FEATURE: SFCC-89, "PDP static product information" — product name, price, description, style code and model line on the product detail page, built as five atoms plus one molecule under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`, wired into a copy-first port of the base PDP page via a `renderHeader` slot on a copy-first port of `product-view`.

## What the plan must deliver

A **sequenced, executable realignment**. Rework of working code is accepted — the developer has explicitly chosen full realignment over surgical fixes. But every step must justify itself against a register row; do not add conformance changes the register did not find.

For each step give: what changes, which files, why (cite the register row), how to verify it, and what could break.

## Hard constraints

1. **Acceptance criteria must survive.** Name, price, description, style code, model line must still render correctly against live SFCC data. Conformance must not cost delivery.
2. **The branch stays green between steps.** Sequence so each step can be verified independently. State the gate command(s) per step.
3. **D1's fix belongs in the atom or molecule, NOT in `productInfo.ts`.** `productInfo.test.ts:70-73` deliberately asserts `price: ''`; changing the mapper breaks a passing test that encodes a considered decision. Design around that.
4. **Three conflicts are the developer's to decide, not yours** — X1 (`var(--zimm-*)` in JSX: rewrite vs move-to-recipe), X2 (must every component have a recipe), X4 (do pages need a story). For each, plan **both** branches with their cost, and mark the step as blocked pending the decision. Do not pick.
5. **Four open items must still appear** in the plan with an owner or a disposition — silently dropping them means the plan optimised for conformance over delivery:
   (a) `c_modelFit` is unpopulated on every catalogue product checked, so the model line never renders;
   (b) the description renders twice — in our content group and in the untouched base `InformationAccordion`, which reads the same `longDescription`;
   (c) translations were deliberately not modified (Tier 2, Integration-owned);
   (d) hero layout metrics (218px column, 180px gap, 140px right margin, gallery aspect ratio) were measured but not applied, because they live inside `product-view`'s layout and applying them would break the "callers byte-identical" guarantee.
6. **Governance:** `overrides/app/routes.tsx` is Tier 2 Global Shell (`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:20`). `overrides/app/components/product-view/` self-labels Tier 2 but is **not** in that file's Shared Product Components list — flag which is wrong rather than assuming. No new packages (Hard Rule #7). No Tier 1 paths.
7. **Do not cite any file under `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/` outside the repo** in the plan text — those are local-only documents that must not reach a PR body, commit message or code comment. Argue from repo-visible evidence (`AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/**`, the code itself).

## Also decide and justify

- **Commit strategy.** D5 says copy-first is bundled with the feature work, and no commits exist yet. Propose the commit sequence — how many commits, what each contains, in what order — such that the copy-first ports land separately from the functional change.
- **Whether D12 (no test proving the ports behave identically) is worth closing**, and if so how, given `vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1 and cannot be widened to run the base's own test files.
- **Where D9's fix belongs** — the `Stack` wrapper in the page, or the atoms.

## Output

A numbered plan, ordered for execution, with a short "risks and what I'd cut first" section at the end. Be concrete: name files, name the gate command for each step. Do not write any file — return the plan as your report.

The scoping error was mine, not the agent's. Separately, the same pass was correct on the locale count where the register was wrong. Moved to NOTE. 74 - "Tier read off imports vs rendered template" resolves the same way for `zimmProductContent` either way. No practical impact. 75

100	| A new package dependency is needed                                           | Stop. No changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
102	| Change affects more than one regional site config                            | Stop. Integration team sign-off required.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
103	| Change spans multiple protection tiers                                       | Stop. Confirm scope with the developer before continuing.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
104	| Requirement is missing, ambiguous, contradictory, or unconfirmed in `.docs/` | Stop. Flag, propose, wait for approval (see Requirements section).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
105	     6	
106	## Multi-site & Routing
107	     8	
108	The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).
109	    10	
110	## Commands
111	    12	
112	- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
113	- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)
114	    15	
115	## Accessibility
116	    17	
117	Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.
118	    19	
119	## Rules
120	    21	
121	*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
122	[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
123	[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
124	(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
125	(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
126	are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*
127	    28	
128	- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
129	- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Local values live in `.env.shared` (tier-independent) and `.env.<tier>` (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) — gitignored, managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; full command reference in `.env.sample`'s header) — and are set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env.sample` tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on its own comment line above the key (value only if it's a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave blank — never a trailing comment, or a blank placeholder reads as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard), (2) run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold the new key into `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>`, then fill in the real value locally. Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.
130	- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
131	- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
132	- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
133	- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
134	- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. Wait for the user to confirm the overrides are rendering before making any functional changes; remove the `console.log` statements once confirmed. Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes.
135	    36	
136	## Consent & Marketing
137	    38	
138	- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
139	- **Marketing opt-in:** Unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked). Sync opt-in state: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.
140	    41	
141	_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._
142	    43	
143	## Type Definitions
144	    45	
145	- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.
146	- **Shared types** (Commerce Cloud entities, API responses, shared hook signatures): `overrides/app/types/` — split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`, re-exported via `index.ts`.
147	- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.
148	    49	
149	## Testing

`globalStyles.ts` is the `.zimm-*` global class registry, composed into

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the

## Co-locating a component's theme file

A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
organisational choice with no runtime difference.

**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.

existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's

file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.

> **Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** This paragraph used to cite `button.ts`'s
> `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as the designer-gated example. That file
> is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above
> routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer
> designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. The example was swapped
> to `header.ts` (genuinely still gated) so this paragraph stops asserting something false.
> Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc
> fix, and is deliberately left open here.

**Enforcement gap, partially closed:** the Tier 1/2 human reviewer was, until this rule
existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's
findings first (14 pre-existing, unrelated violations turned up the day it was built) before
turning it into a hard gate.

**Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one
split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g.
`footerShared.ts`, holding the breakpoints and the one size value `footerNavColumn.css.ts`
and `bottomBar.css.ts` both need. Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files;
that's exactly the drift risk "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" (above)
already warns about.

**Reference example:** the footer decomposition (SFCC-55 follow-up) split
`theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts across `footer/footer.css.ts` (shell),
`footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, and
three `ui-kits/organisms/`/`ui-kits/molecules/` recipes — with `footerShared.ts` left
behind in `theme/components/` for the two genuinely cross-file values.

## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)

- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
- `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `zimmButton.css.ts`,
  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Runs the BrowserStack Automate suite scoped to one Jira story, the same
     3	# way e2e-browserstack does on a PR — lets a developer execute their
     4	# feature-branch story locally before pushing, using real BrowserStack
     5	# (see .claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping).
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   npm run test:story                  # auto-detects the Jira key(s)
     9	#   npm run test:story -- SFCC-142      # explicit key(s), space-separated
    10	#
    11	# Auto-detection scans commit messages on this branch (commits ahead of
    12	# origin/develop) and the branch name for SFCC-NNN — the same SFCC-[0-9]+
    13	# pattern qa.yml's "Detect Jira story keys" step uses for a PR's title/body/
    14	# branch. Kept as a literal duplicate there rather than a shared script:
    15	# it's one regex, and the input sources genuinely differ (PR text vs local
    16	# git state) — update both if the Jira project key prefix ever changes.
    17	#
    18	# Exit code: 0 if BrowserStack ran (regardless of test pass/fail — that's
    19	# BrowserStack's own exit code), 1 if no Jira key was found or a required
    20	# env var is missing.
    21	
    22	set -euo pipefail
    23	
    24	ENV_FILE=".env"
    25	
    26	if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
    27	    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    28	    set -a && source "$ENV_FILE" && set +a
    29	fi
    30	
    31	KEYS="$*"
    32	
    33	if [[ -z "$KEYS" ]]; then
    34	    BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/develop 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    35	    if [[ -n "$BASE" ]]; then
    36	        COMMIT_MSGS=$(git log "$BASE"..HEAD --pretty=%B 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    37	    else
    38	        COMMIT_MSGS=""
    39	    fi
    40	    BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
    41	    # grep exits 1 on no match, which would otherwise abort the script here
    42	    # under set -e/pipefail before the "no key found" message below can run.
    43	    KEYS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$COMMIT_MSGS" "$BRANCH" | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' || true)
    44	fi
    45	
    46	KEYS=$(echo "$KEYS" | xargs -n1 | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
    47	
    48	if [[ -z "$KEYS" ]]; then
    49	    echo "No Jira story key found." >&2
    50	    echo "Pass one explicitly: npm run test:story -- SFCC-142" >&2
    51	    echo "(auto-detection looks for SFCC-NNN in commit messages on this branch and the branch name)" >&2
    52	    exit 1
    53	fi
    54	
    55	MISSING=()
    56	for var in BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY RETAIL_APP_HOME PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD; do
    57	    if [[ -z "${!var:-}" ]]; then
    58	        MISSING+=("$var")
    59	    fi
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    63	    echo "Missing required env var(s): ${MISSING[*]}" >&2
    64	    echo "Set these in .env — see .env.sample for the full list this needs." >&2
    65	    exit 1
    66	fi
    67	
    68	GREP=$(echo "$KEYS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/@/' | paste -sd '|')
    69	
    70	echo "Running BrowserStack for: $KEYS (--grep \"$GREP\")"
    71	
    72	export SPRINT_NUMBER="${SPRINT_NUMBER:-local-$(whoami)-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)}"
    73	export SITE_ID="${SITE_ID:-au}"
    74	
    75	npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "$GREP"

     2	# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
     3	#
     4	# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
     5	#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
     6	
     7	commit_msg=$(cat "$1")
     8	
     9	# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
    10	if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
    11	  exit 0
    12	fi
    13	
    14	# Conventional commits pattern
    15	# type(optional-scope): description
    16	# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
    17	pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
    18	
    19	if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then

    21	  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
    22	  echo ""
    23	  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
    24	  echo ""
    25	  echo "  Types:"
    26	  echo "    feat           new feature"
    27	  echo "    fix            bug fix"

     2	# Pre-commit hook:
     3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
     4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
     5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
     6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
     7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
     8	#
     9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
    10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
    11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
    12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
    14	
    15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
    17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
    18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
    19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
    20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21	
    22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
    24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
    25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
    26	
    27	  # fnm
    28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
    30	  fi
    31	
    32	  # volta
    33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
    35	  fi
    36	
    37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    40	    exit 1
    41	  fi
    42	fi
    43	
    44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
    46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48	
    49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
    50	
    51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
    52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
    53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
    54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
    55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
    56	
    57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
    58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
    59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
    60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
    61	  git add .claude/registry/
    62	fi
    63	
    64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
    66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
    67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
    68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
    69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    70	
    71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
    72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    74	    || true)

    76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    78	    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
    79	      echo ""
    80	      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
     3	#
     4	# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
     5	# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
     6	# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
     7	# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
     8	#
     9	# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
    10	#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
    11	#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
    12	# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
    13	#
    14	# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
    15	#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
    16	# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
    17	# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
    18	# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
    19	# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
    20	rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
    21	final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
    22	status=0
    23	
    24	while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
    25	  case "$remote_ref" in
    26	    refs/tags/v*)
    27	      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
    28	      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
    29	        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
    30	        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
    31	        status=1
    32	      fi
    33	      ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done
    36	
    37	exit $status

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
     3	#
     4	# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
     5	# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
     6	# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
     7	# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
     8	#
     9	# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
    10	#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
    11	#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
    12	# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
    13	#
    14	# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
    15	#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
    16	# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
    17	# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
    18	# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
    19	# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
    20	rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
    21	final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
    22	status=0
    23	
    24	while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
    25	  case "$remote_ref" in
    26	    refs/tags/v*)
    27	      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
    28	      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
    29	        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
    30	        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
    31	        status=1
    32	      fi
    33	      ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done

content.content:
- Contentful Studio integration (pointing to mock account)
- **Contentful content model tooling** (`npm run sync:contentful` / `npm run install:contentful`) — authors `scripts/contentful/content-types/` as one organization-scoped Environment Template and installs it per environment via the Management API (replaced the earlier per-environment sync.js + migrations pipeline, 2026-08-23).
- **ShoppableImage component decommissioned** (2026-08-23) — it was a Studio Experience component + standard content type synced 2026-05-11, but had 0 entries and was removed (content type, React component, and its hotspotMarker/hotspotPopup sub-components) once the region/link/footerConfig content model landed. `CollectionHero` and `ImageText` are the remaining Studio Experience components.
- Basic SFCC Commerce SDK integration (pointing to mock account)
- Home page / home-preview page merged
- Functional requirements signed off (Checkout, Returns, Orders, Payments, Cart, Regional, Content, PDP/PLP, Search, CRM)
- Design token foundation ported from the F2R Handover into `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` (`colour.ts`, `typography.ts`, `gridSystem.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `sizes.ts`, `motion.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`) plus the `.zimm-*` global classes in `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`; composed in `overrides/app/theme/index.ts`, per-component overrides now co-located beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` and registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (`theme/components/` itself now holds only `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` as registered recipes, plus `navConstants.ts` and `footerShared.ts` for values shared across split-out files). Delivered as a foundation for the manual UI build (branch `feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev`); F2R component work continues separately on `feature/f2r-component-registry` and `feature/f2r-implementation-workflow`. Futura Round **is** self-hosted as of SFCC-55 — two faces (400/500) ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` and are served on every tier. Open with the UI designer: primary-action hover contrast (2.96:1), inverse focus ring, and button-height / nav letter-spacing deviations from the Handover.
- **Token architecture hardened** (2026-08-18): `zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry) is now fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files via imports instead of hand-duplicated literals, closing the drift risk the original port above carried. `typography.ts` gained a proper `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights` scale layer. `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem (WCAG 1.4.4); within those two files, px is kept only for hairline geometry (border widths, focus-ring offsets — now named tokens in `spacing.ts`'s `focusRingOffsets`). `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding constants are a separate, already-flagged px exception (not hairline geometry) — see below. `zimmButton.css.ts` is now the single source of truth for button styling — `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*`/`.zimm-text-btn-*` classes (different heights, transparent-vs-opaque secondary background, zero interactive states) were removed entirely; any button must use Chakra's `<Button>`, never a class. `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` convention (no direct `foundation/` imports, no Chakra semantic colour-token names). New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the styling-source hierarchy, unit rules, the alias-is-a-reference-not-a-copy principle, and a real gotcha: importing an already-overridden component via the SFCC base path resolves correctly in the real app but silently renders the unstyled base version in Storybook/Vitest (the `ccExtensibility` resolver is webpack-only, neither tool loads it). Still open, flagged inline rather than silently resolved: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px prototype values) disagree with the Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all — both pending UI-designer sign-off.
- **Header override** (`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`): two-row layout, brand logo via `BrandLogo` component (overrides base SVG at `overrides/app/assets/svg/brand-logo.svg`), uppercase nav with `::after` hover animation, Account/Saved/Bag text buttons with matching animation, chevrons hidden. Still being refined visually against Figma.
- Path aliases (`~` → root, `app` → `overrides/app`) wired up across Babel, tsconfig, Storybook, and Jest
- **Per-tier environment switching** (`npm run env` → `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`) — manages `.env.shared` / `.env.<tier>` across dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod via `init` (scaffold + pull + Contentful auto-fetch), `validate [--live]` (structural checks plus live Contentful Delivery API + SFCC SLAS guest-token calls), and `push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only). Shared/tier values (excluding personal credentials) can be centrally published through this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per tier) — write gated to repo Admin. Landed 2026-07-13.

## In Progress
- **SFCC-55 global footer** (PR #59): footer decomposed into `overrides/app/components/footer/` plus
  `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/`, most with a co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe registered in
  `theme/components/index.ts`. `FooterContainer` fetches live Contentful `footerConfig` client-side and
  resolves per-storefront content via `utils/resolveByRegion.ts`. Microcopy comes from the `uiCopy` content
  type through `useUiCopy` (Context provider mounted in `_app-config`). Open items: the footer is not in the
  SSR HTML (client-only `useEffect` fetch, no `getProps`); no locale is passed to Contentful, so all
  storefronts currently receive the space default; and `en-CA` — which `SITE_LOCALES` lists for
  ZimmermannUSIntl — is now in `bootstrapSpace.mjs`'s locale list, but whether the **live** space has it
  is still unconfirmed from the repo. Re-running `setup:contentful` is what would provision it; until
  someone does, `/en-ca/` Experience pages still send an unknown locale to the CDA.
- **Header visual refinement**: layout and animations are implemented; still being iterated against the draft Figma to close remaining gaps

## What's Pending
- All integrations need to point to production accounts (SFCC, Contentful)
- Global-e integration (confirm pricing flow mechanism before implementing)
- Didomi consent management (implement per storefront defaults in REG-054)
- Omneo / Emarsys marketing sync
- Adyen payment integration
- MuleSoft middleware connections
- PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout flows
- BOPIS (Collect in Boutique) checkout flow
- Full multi-site routing — 8 SFCC sites across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME). **US site topology updated (REG-005, 2026-07-10):** US splits into two separate SFCC sites — US domestic (`/us/`, SFCC checkout) and US international (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout). New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
- Address autocomplete via Google Maps API

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Storybook interaction + a11y tests — runs on every PR to develop
  # and release/**. Exercises play() functions and @storybook/addon-a11y
  # component-level checks headless. Runs in parallel with unit-tests.
  # Runner: @storybook/test-runner (Playwright-based). Storybook is built
  # to storybook-static/, served by http-server, tested by test-storybook.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  storybook-test:
    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
        env:
          CI: true

      - name: Upload Storybook test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: storybook-test-results

content.content: # Components, Hooks & Storybook Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). --- ## Components - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). No default exports of anonymous functions. - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. - **Props type placement:** - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with other shared types worth co-locating. - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. - **JSDoc** is required on: - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). - Any exported hook. - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions for "I forgot to mark it optional." - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get these right at authoring time:** - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to announce. - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). --- ## Composition — writing a "clean" component Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline state belongs in a custom hook instead. - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new dependency needed). - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container component, which then passes the result down. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). --- ## Components - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). No step depends on a later step to become green. --- ## Governance finding — resolve before writing code **`overrides/app/components/product-view/` self-labels a tier that nothing enforces. The self-label is what's wrong, not the lists.** Four repo-visible sources, all consistent with each other and none with the comment: - `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:29-36` — the Shared Product Components list is `product-tile`, `product-item`, `display-price`, `image-gallery`, `swatch-group`, `recommended-products`. Not `product-view`. - `CODEOWNERS:96-104` — mirrors that list exactly. There is **no CODEOWNERS entry of any kind** matching `overrides/app/components/product-view/`, and no default `*` owner line, so no reviewer is auto-requested for it. - `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml:209-215` — the `tier2` changed-files glob omits it, so the Tier 2 warning comment will not fire on this PR. - `.claude/registry/components.md:54` — classifies `ProductView` as `4 — Feature-local`, owner `Shared`. (Corroboration only, not independent: `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:199`'s `getTier()` derives the column from the rules files.) Against that, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:19` states *"Tier 2 (Shared Product Components, owner Squad B — see .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md)."* It cites a document that does not say it. **Disposition:** correct the comment in Step 1. A comment claiming a protection the tooling does not apply is worse than no comment — a reviewer trusts it and skips the check they'd otherwise make. Separately raise, **not in this branch**, whether `product-view/` should be *promoted* into `protectedFiles.md` + `CODEOWNERS` + the workflow glob; four base modules import it, which is a wider blast radius than several directories already on the list. That is a three-file governance change needing both squads and is not SFCC-89's to make. Second, related fact the register's PR-body note doesn't cover: `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` **is** Tier 2 (`protectedFiles.md:46-51`, `CODEOWNERS:117` → `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers`, and the workflow's `overrides/app/theme/components/**` glob). Registering the recipes there is mandatory (`protectedFiles.md:53`), so this PR carries **two** Tier 2 files, not one. Both must be declared. Third, reviewer-routing note: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is Squad B per `CODEOWNERS:162` but appears in `.claude/rules/squadA.md`'s territory list. This is already logged as a known conflict at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Known gaps" section — flag it in the PR body so the right squad reviews; do not try to settle it here. --- ## Step 0 — Preserve the working tree before restructuring (prerequisite) **What:** The 29 staged files are the only copy of this work and there are no commits. Steps 1–2 require *reconstructing* two of them in a reduced form, which means editing working code backwards. **Do:** create a scratch branch holding the current tree verbatim, e.g. commit the 29 staged files once onto `sfcc-89-wip` (never pushed), then return to `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` reset to `8362b3c`. **Why:** `git checkout sfcc-89-wip -- ` then restores any file byte-exactly, so the "reduced port then full port" sequence cannot silently drift. It also gives an invariant to check at the end of Step 8: `git diff sfcc-89-wip --stat` must show *only* the realignment deltas listed below and nothing else. **Gate:** `git diff sfcc-89-wip` is empty immediately after creating it. **What could break:** nothing — but `.husky/pre-commit` → `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:49-62` regenerates and auto-stages `.claude/registry/` on any commit touching `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}` or `routes.tsx`. Expect a registry delta in most commits below; that's the hook working, don't fight it. --- ## Step 1 — Reduce the two ports to faithful copy-first ports **Register row:** D5 (copy-first bundled with functional change; `AGENTS.md:134` — *"Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes"*). Also D4 and the "full original prop surface" claim. **Files:** - `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` — remove `renderHeader` from `ProductViewProps` (line 163), remove its default in the destructuring (line 267), restore the two call sites at lines 676 and 729 to the base's direct `` form. - `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — remove the SFCC-89 import block (lines 67-71), `formatPrice`, `renderStaticProductHeader`, `staticInfo`, the `renderHeader=` prop on `` (line 864), and the `` block (lines 881-884). **Also in this step — two corrections to the port itself:** 1. **Fix the tier comment** at `product-view/index.tsx:19` per the governance finding above. 2. **Add the two missing base props.** Base `ProductView.propTypes` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx:1019-1051`) declares `promotionId: PropTypes.string` and `alignItems: PropTypes.string`; our `ProductViewProps` (lines 117-164) omits both. `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:473,477` actually passes both to ``. Neither is read by the base body and the port destructures a fixed list with no rest spread, so **runtime behaviour is identical either way** — but the file's own header claims "full original prop surface", and today that claim is false at two props. Add `promotionId?: string;` and `alignItems?: string;`. **Why here and not later:** the port commit is the one that must be able to say "faithful". Adding the props in a later commit makes the port commit's claim retroactively wrong. **Gates:** G1, G2, G3, G4, G5 (G5 will read 19 until Step 2). **What could break:** removing `renderHeader` must not disturb the surrounding JSX indentation at 676/729 — the base has *two* header call sites (mobile and desktop) and missing one leaves the PDP with a duplicated or absent header when Step 4 re-adds the slot. Verify both are restored by diffing the reduced port's header regions against `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx`. --- ## Step 2 — Acknowledge the five ported raw literals **Register row:** D3. Takes the repo 19 → 14. Explicitly **not** a regression we introduced — the docs already count these five and name the file — so the commit message and PR body must frame it as *an improvement now available*, not a fix. **File:** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` only. **Where exactly** (the acknowledgement window in `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:119-122` is the contiguous non-blank block of lines *ending at the match*, so placement matters): | Match | Blank line above at | Put the comment at | |---|---|---| | `'120px'` ×3, lines 722-724 | 715 | extend the existing JSX comment on line 716, or add a second `{/* … */}` line at 717 | | `'32px'`, line 775 | far above | a `//` line directly above `const content = image ? (` (line 771) — plain TS statement position, unambiguously valid | | `'200px'`, line 833 | 831 | a `{/* … */}` line at 832, immediately above `{!isProductASet && …` — JSX children position, so it must be `{/* */}`, not `//` | **Wording:** use the explicit `audit-allow:` marker with the base citation, e.g. `audit-allow: verbatim from the base product-view (index.jsx:636-638); the copy-first rule requires it unchanged.` Avoid the words *provisional / pending / placeholder* here — `EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE` (line 59) matches them too, and using them would wrongly imply a designer sign-off is outstanding. **Gates:** G5 → **14 unacknowledged**. Then G1, G3, G4 (comments only; nothing else can move). **What could break:** a stray blank line between the comment and the match silently un-acknowledges it. Re-run G5 and read the acknowledged list, not just the count. --- ## → COMMIT 1 — `refactor(product-view): copy-first TypeScript port of product-view and product-detail` Contents: Steps 1 + 2, plus `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` and `overrides/app/routes.tsx`. **Why `routes.tsx` belongs in the copy-first commit, not the feature commit:** the port's own comment (`routes.tsx:26-32`) is correct that without the explicit route the override is dead code and the base page renders. `AGENTS.md:134` step 4 requires the developer to *confirm the override is rendering* before any functional change — that confirmation is physically impossible without the route. The route is therefore part of the copy-first step. The alternative (routes.tsx as its own commit, so the one Tier 2 Global Shell file has an isolated diff) is defensible; I'd take the atomic version because it makes the commit independently runnable, and name `routes.tsx` in the commit body so the Tier 2 touch is still obvious. **Verification before moving on:** G1–G5 all green, **plus G6 showing the *base* PDP rendering through the TypeScript override** — same output as develop, no Zimmermann content. If the copy-first `console.log` markers were already removed (the register records they are), and the developer has not yet done this confirmation, re-add them temporarily and strip them before committing; record in the PR body that step 4 was performed. --- ## Step 3 — Re-add the `renderHeader` slot **Register row:** D4. The bridge rule's literal wording is "full original prop surface", which an additive optional prop with a behaviour-preserving default satisfies — the register calls this a judgement call, not a break. Isolating it in one commit is what makes that judgement reviewable. **File:** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` only — restore the `renderHeader?: (props: ProductViewHeaderProps) => React.ReactNode` member with its JSDoc, the default `renderHeader = (headerProps) => ` at line 267, and the two `renderHeader({...})` call sites at 676/729. **Why the default matters and must be stated in the commit body:** it is the entire argument that `product-view-modal/index.jsx:17`, `product-view-modal/bundle.jsx:21`, `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:22` and `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:41` are unaffected — none of them passes `renderHeader`, so all four get byte-identical output. **Gates:** G1, G2, G3, G4. **What could break:** if the default is omitted or the two call sites diverge, three base flows lose their header. Step 5 (D12) is what stops this regressing later. ## → COMMIT 2 — `feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content` --- ## Step 4 — Land the ui-kit components, with D1, D2, D9 and D10 folded in The bug rows are folded into the commit that authors the code rather than added as follow-up "fix" commits. The register is a pre-commit review; no commit should ever contain a defect that was known before the first commit existed. ### 4a — D1: the price atom must collapse when there is nothing to show **Register row:** D1. Constraint honoured: **nothing in `productInfo.ts` changes.** `productInfo.test.ts:70-73` keeps asserting `price: ''`, and the mapper's contract ("only `name` is load-bearing") is untouched. **File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx`. **Change:** after the `useStyleConfig` call, `if (!price) return null;`. Widen the prop to `price?: string` and update the JSDoc. **Hook ordering is load-bearing:** the guard must come *after* `useStyleConfig('ZimmProductPrice', { variant })` on line 20, never before it. An early return above the hook is a conditional hook call and will add a `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` error, moving G3 off the 17-error baseline. This is exactly the order `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:18-19` and `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:27-29` already use. **Why the atom and not the molecule:** four of the five atoms already self-collapse. Making price the fifth restores the base header's own behaviour (`product-view/index.jsx` renders `DisplayPrice` only when `priceData?.currentPrice` is truthy), gives the atom the same contract as its siblings, and means any *future* direct consumer of `ZimmProductPrice` cannot reintroduce the bug. Guarding in the molecule instead would put the emptiness rule in the parent — the precise thing `zimmProductContent.css.ts:9-13` already argues against. **New/changed tests:** - New `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx`, mirroring the three existing atom tests: renders for a formatted string, renders nothing for `''` and `undefined`. The CONFORMS row's rule is "a test file per branching atom" — price becomes the fourth branching atom, so it acquires the fourth test. - New story `zimmProductPrice/index.stories.tsx` → *"Absent — collapses"*, `play` asserting `queryByTestId('product-price')` is null. - New story `zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx` → *"Without price — rhythm collapses"*, `play` asserting `root.children` has length 2 and `getComputedStyle(root).rowGap === '20px'`. **This is the direct proof of the doubled-gap fix** and mirrors the existing `WithoutDescription` story's shape exactly (lines 47-68). ### 4b — D9: a self-collapsing container for the model line and style code **Register row:** D9. **Where the fix belongs — decided:** **the wrapper, not the atoms — and expressed as a recipe on a molecule, not as a predicate in the page.** The atoms cannot be the fix: they already return `null` and a child cannot suppress its parent.
